sources.title: Unified Telemetry Strategy for Data Centers
sources.not_available: Pages 5–16 named in the contents are absent. Their technical content was not reviewed or inferred.

supported_claims.claim: A shared time-series layer can sit beside existing facility systems and support historical incident investigation.
The proposed vendor stack uses Telegraf and InfluxDB 3 Enterprise and addresses both operators and equipment/software suppliers.
BMS supplies cooling/environment context, EPMS electrical context and DCIM inventory/rack/ownership context.

sources.title: Data Center Telemetry in the AI Era
sources.use: Supplementary motivation for cross-layer observations, clock alignment and sampling-resolution comparisons. Vendor performance and outage claims are not model calibration.
Line-protocol escaping, typed fields, timestamp precision and identity. Duplicate overwrite order must not be relied upon.
Motivation for bounded-buffer loss and recovery planning. Capacity calculations count scalar observations and are not a benchmark of Telegraf's multi-field metric buffering.

implementation_extensions: Canonical history envelopes, strict conflict policy and time-valid context
Composed terminal-power, cooling and thermal-zone scenarios
Synthetic sampling, quality, clock and topology analysis
Storage, buffer, triage labor and discounted cash-flow sensitivities

assumptions.source_of_all_numerical_defaults: Project-selected synthetic engineering assumptions; not figures extracted from the PDF.
assumptions.rack_power: 20 kW idle, 100 kW peak, 800 V DC terminal; baseline utilization 0.5
assumptions.cooling: 120 kW thermal capacity, 20 kW during failure, COP 5, 500 kJ/K mixed thermal capacitance; no CFD or pump hydraulic calibration
assumptions.utility_sag: 230 to 195 V RMS L1-N for 60 seconds, ideal UPS protection assumed
assumptions.economic_currency: EUR; no product pricing, taxes, financing, escalation or measured avoided downtime
assumptions.storage: 100 bytes per observation and 160 per aggregate are placeholders requiring deployment measurement

limitations: Offline reference implementation; no live BMS, EPMS, DCIM or InfluxDB integration is claimed.
Event ordering does not establish root cause; possible topology exposure does not establish customer impact.
No standards compliance, predictive maintenance accuracy or availability guarantee.
The supplied PDF is not redistributed.
